anomaly_def.Name: Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly : Engine and background components consume more physical memory and swap than the host can safely provide, causing OS-level memory pressure and database OOM or eviction events.
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly : Sessions serialize on hot buffer pages, latches, or I/O slots, leading to excessive buffer-busy waits, CPU spin, and stalled page access.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : Client-to-server transport, listener, socket, or connection-pool resources saturate, producing slow or failed connects and prolonged client I/O waits.

When these three root causes strike simultaneously, the database shows a convoluted mix of symptoms: resident-set size and swap continually rise while CPU usage swings between spin waits on buffer latches and idle time caused by blocked or disconnected clients. Wait-event dashboards light up with alternating memory-pressure stalls, buffer latch waits, and client read/write or connection establishment waits. Checkpoint and dirty-page flush latency grows because hot pages linger in memory under contention, further bloating memory with dirty buffers. Meanwhile, clients experience erratic query latencies, intermittent "too many connections" or timeout errors, and retransmissions on the network as over-subscribed back-ends struggle to send or receive data that must first be fetched from an overcommitted, latch-contended buffer pool.

Causal chain: memory over-allocation inflates each backend’s footprint and shrinks effective buffer cache, forcing heavier churn and making individual pages hotter; this magnifies latch contention and CPU spin. The prolonged execution times that result keep sessions and their sockets open longer, which raises connection counts and floods listener backlogs, pushing the system toward the network/connectivity limit. Conversely, slow or reset network links leave server backends blocked in client I/O, holding buffer pins and memory allocations alive, which further tightens memory pressure and extends latch hold times. The reinforcing loop among memory exhaustion, buffer-level serialization, and stalled network endpoints amplifies resource starvation across all tiers, threatening systemic throughput collapse and potential node eviction or crash.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds to wait for more data from a source/replica connection before aborting the read.
entry.trigger_condition: A replica waits longer than replica_net_timeout for more data from the source connection.
entry.workload_impact: The replication network read is aborted and the replica considers the connection interrupted.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL replication system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
